imageAlt: Male stag beetle viewed from above

distribution.text: Found across much of Europe, including southern Britain. Records also extend into parts of western Asia.

facts.habitat: Woodland edges, hedgerows, orchards, parks and gardens

overview.text: Male stag beetles have enlarged jaws resembling antlers, which they use in contests with other males. Their larvae develop underground and feed on decaying wood.

imageAlt: Male titan beetle viewed from above

distribution.text: Recorded in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, the Guianas and northern Brazil, in tropical rainforest.

overview.text: The titan beetle is a giant longhorn beetle inhabiting tropical forests in South America. It is notable for its enormous body, powerful jaws and defensive spines.

distribution.text: Native to Europe and parts of Asia and Africa. Introduced populations are established in the United States.

facts.habitat: Gardens, grassland, woodland and other habitats with aphids

overview.text: The seven-spot ladybird is a small, aphid-eating beetle recognised by seven black spots on its red wing covers. It occurs in varied habitats, including parks and gardens.
